messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than before—less like a storm gathering, more like a machine running on borrowed time. The gears still turn, but the hands on the clock don’t quite match up anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quieter, and even the traders are still moving goods, though the roads are rough. But the slowdowns in the capital aren’t just traffic, and the gaps in the offices tell a story the news won’t. Stay sharp, not scared—this calm may not last, and the wrong word could still cost us everything."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, supplies running low, and even the birds seem to be leaving early. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case the storm hits sooner than expected. Stay sharp, but don’t draw attention—we’ll talk more when the air clears."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm, not the calm after. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush. The walls are still standing, but the foundation is shifting beneath them."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm enough that people are leaving their windows open, but the wind still carries whispers of storms. The pharmacist down the street says business is steady, though he’s been stocking up on basics just in case. No need to panic, but maybe keep an eye on the horizon."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just shifting winds. The old guard is digging in, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. Still, we should keep our coats close and watch the skies, just in case."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unseasonably warm in some places, but the old patterns still hold. The farmers are watching the fields closely, and the markets are quiet, but the songs in the streets tell a different story. No one’s rushing, but no one’s sleeping soundly either. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked—just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like a storm holding its breath. The usual signs are there, but nothing yet to say which way the wind will blow. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the pause before a storm, not the calm after. The usual rules seem suspended, but no one knows if this is the beginning of the end or just another test of loyalty. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time for bold moves, only quiet preparation."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s settled into a steady pattern—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for now. The usual whispers still drift around, but even the most cautious vendors have reopened their stalls without a second thought. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for today, the air feels lighter than it has in months."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a held breath. The usual signs are there, but the rhythm is off, like a clock winding down. Let’s stay sharp, but not too loud—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who tip the balance."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less fear, more quiet energy. The regime’s still strong, but even the walls seem to be listening now. Let’s stay sharp, but keep the doors open."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier—like the pause before a storm. Small things are shifting, but nothing is certain yet. Stay sharp, but keep your circle tight."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually still, but the barometer’s dropping. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case the rain comes sideways. No need to rush, but don’t be caught unprepared."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the quiet before something unplanned. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks aren’t in the walls yet; they’re in the way people are starting to look at each other. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The gardeners are still pruning the roses, but a few have noticed the soil’s getting drier, and the birds aren’t singing as loudly as they used to. Best to keep the windows open, but not too wide."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like the calm before a storm, more like the quiet of a machine running out of fuel, but no one’s sure if it’ll sputter or explode. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, but not yet set in stone."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The usual signs are still there, but the rhythm is off, and no one’s sure if the next step will be a stumble or a steadying hand. Keep your eyes open, your plans ready, and your words measured—this isn’t the time for recklessness, but neither is it the time to assume the quiet will last."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints are quieter, the borders are open, and even the censors seem distracted. But don’t mistake ease for safety; the system is still standing, just wobbling. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—payments are late, the streets too quiet, and even the guards seem to be holding their breath. No one knows which way the wind will blow, but the cracks are showing, and the regime’s grip isn’t as sure as it pretends."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—people are talking, but the walls still listen. The regime’s moves suggest both caution and calculation, so let’s stay sharp, not reckless. We’ll know more when the next step is taken, not before."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack them away just yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts, but the old patterns still hold in some places. The market’s quieter than usual, though a few familiar faces seem to be packing up early. Keep an eye on the usual spots, but don’t assume the usual rules apply. Stay sharp, stay safe."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip, more like the quiet before a storm. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing, and the question isn’t *if* something shifts, but *what* will tip it first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
